title: Metabolic Analysis of Mouse Bone-Marrow-Derived Dendritic Cells Using an Extracellular Flux Analyzer
author: Gotoh, Takata, et al.
materials: Seahorse XF Cell Mito Stress Test Kit

steps.title: Prepare RBC Lysis Solution
steps.instruction: Make 0.16 M NH₄Cl solution (8.3 g NH₄Cl in 1 L dH₂O) and 0.17 M Tris‑HCl solution (20.6 g Trizma·HCl in 1 L dH₂O, pH 7.65). Mix 90 mL of the NH₄Cl solution with 10 mL of the Tris solution, adjust pH to 7.2 with HCl/NaCl, sterilize with bottle‑top filters and store at 2–8 °C.

steps.title: Prepare RPMI Culture Medium
steps.instruction: To 430 mL RPMI add 10 % (v/v) fetal bovine serum (50 mL), 1 % (v/v) penicillin‑streptomycin (5 mL, 10 000 U mL⁻¹), 1 % (v/v) L‑glutamine (5 mL, 29.2 mg mL⁻¹), 1 % (v/v) non‑essential amino acids (5 mL, 100×), 1 % (v/v) sodium pyruvate (5 mL, 100 mM), and 0.5 mL 2‑mercaptoethanol (50 mM) to a final volume of 500 mL. Mix well and keep sterile.

steps.title: Prepare XF Assay Media (Mitochondrial Stress)
steps.instruction: Warm 97 mL XF RPMI assay medium (pH 7.4) to 37 °C, add 1 mL 1.0 M glucose (final 10 mM), 1 mL 100 mM pyruvate (final 1 mM) and 1 mL 200 mM glutamine (final 2 mM). Adjust pH to 7.4, filter, keep at 37 °C without CO₂ until use (use within 4 h).

steps.title: Prepare XF Assay Media (Glycolysis Stress)
steps.instruction: Warm 98 mL XF RPMI assay medium (pH 7.4) to 37 °C, add 1 mL 100 mM pyruvate (final 1 mM) and 1 mL 200 mM glutamine (final 2 mM). Adjust pH to 7.4, filter, keep at 37 °C without CO₂ until use.

steps.title: Prepare XF Assay Media (Palmitate Oxidation)
steps.instruction: Warm 98 mL XF RPMI assay medium (pH 7.4) to 37 °C, add 1 mL 1.0 M glucose (final 10 mM) and 1 mL 200 mM glutamine (final 2 mM). Adjust pH to 7.4, filter, keep at 37 °C without CO₂ until use.

steps.title: Prepare TLR‑Induced XF Media
steps.instruction: Dissolve 8.4 g RPMI‑1640 powder (without glucose and sodium bicarbonate) in dH₂O to 1000 mL, add 10 % (v/v) FBS (100 mL), 1 % (v/v) sodium pyruvate (10 mL, 100 mM) and D‑glucose to 1000 mg L⁻¹ (890 mL dH₂O). Adjust pH to 7.4, sterilize, store at 2–8 °C and use within 4 h.

steps.title: Prepare Inhibitor Stock Solutions
steps.instruction: Make 10 mM oligomycin stock (5 mg in DMSO, 632 µL), 100 mM FCCP stock (10 mg in DMSO, 393 µL), 10 mM rotenone stock (5 mg in DMSO, 1267 µL) and 10 mM antimycin‑A stock (5 mg in DMSO, 393 µL). Store stocks at –20 °C protected from light.

steps.title: Prepare Palmitate‑BSA Conjugate
steps.instruction: Prepare 0.34 mM BSA solution: dissolve 2.267 g BSA in 100 mL 150 mM NaCl (37 °C, stir until clear). Prepare 2.5 mM PA solution: dissolve 30.6 mg sodium palmitate in 44 mL 150 mM NaCl (70 °C, stir until clear, keep ≥50 °C). Conjugate: warm 50 mL 150 mM NaCl (37 °C), add PA solution in eight 5 mL aliquots over 1 h while stirring at 37 °C, then add 10 mL 150 mM NaCl, bring volume to 100 mL, adjust pH to 7.4, aliquot 2–5 mL, freeze at –20 °C.

steps.title: Isolate Mouse Bone Marrow Cells
steps.instruction: Euthanize a male 6–10‑week mouse with CO₂ or isoflurane, spray skin with 70 % ethanol, dissect femurs and tibias into PBS, remove muscle, trim bone ends, flush marrow with 5 mL PBS using a 5 mL syringe with 21‑G needle into a 60‑mm dish, pipette up/down three times, collect suspension, optionally filter through 70‑µm strainer, centrifuge 3000 rpm (800 g) 4 °C 5 min, discard supernatant, add 1 mL RBC‑lysis buffer per mouse, mix 30–60 s, dilute with 10 mL RPMI, centrifuge again 3000 rpm 4 °C 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 10 mL RPMI, keep on ice, count cells (2–6 × 10⁷ total).

steps.title: Culture Bone‑Marrow‑Derived Dendritic Cells
steps.instruction: Day 0: seed 2 × 10⁶ bone‑marrow cells in 2 mL RPMI + 10–25 ng mL⁻¹ GM‑CSF in a 12‑well plate (37 °C, 5 % CO₂). Day 3 and Day 5: add 2 mL fresh RPMI + GM‑CSF to each well and split each well into two. Day 6–7: harvest non‑adherent DCs (1–3 × 10⁷ cells per mouse), avoiding highly adherent cells.

steps.title: Purify CD11c⁺ Dendritic Cells (MACS)
steps.instruction: Resuspend harvested DCs in 10 mL MACS buffer, centrifuge 3000 rpm 4 °C 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 400 µL MACS buffer per 1–2 × 10⁸ cells, add 100 µL CD11c MicroBeads UltraPure per 1–2 × 10⁸ cells, mix, incubate 10 min on ice (2–8 °C) in the dark, add 10 mL MACS buffer, centrifuge 3000 rpm 4 °C 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 1 mL MACS buffer, place LS column in magnetic separator, rinse with 3 mL MACS buffer, apply cell suspension, wash column three times with 3 mL MACS buffer, remove column, place on a 15 mL collection tube, flush CD11c⁺ cells with 5 mL MACS buffer using the plunger. Optional: assess purity by flow cytometry.

steps.title: Coat XF Plate with Poly‑Lysine
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 0.01 % poly‑L‑lysine (or poly‑D‑lysine) to each well of a 24‑well XF cell‑culture plate, tap to cover the bottom, incubate ≥5 min at room temperature, aspirate solution, rinse wells thoroughly with sterile water, and dry the plate ≥2 h before seeding cells.

steps.title: Seed Cells for TLR Metabolic Assay
steps.instruction: Stimulate BMDCs with LPS 100 ng mL⁻¹ or CpG‑DNA 1 µM for ≥12 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Harvest cells, centrifuge 3000 rpm 4 °C 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in XF assay medium at 2 × 10⁶ mL⁻¹, seed 100 µL per PLL‑coated well (no blank), centrifuge plate 2000 rpm 2–5 min at room temperature, add 400 µL XF assay medium to each sample well and 500 µL to the blank well, incubate 30–60 min at 37 °C without CO₂ before loading onto the XF24 analyzer.

steps.title: Seed Cells for Fatty‑Acid Oxidation Assay
steps.instruction: Harvest BMDCs as above, resuspend in XF assay medium at 2 × 10⁶ mL⁻¹, seed 100 µL per PLL‑coated well, centrifuge 2000 rpm 2–5 min RT, add 400 µL XF assay medium containing either 0.3 mM PA + 0.05 mM BSA, 0.05 mM BSA alone, or 200 µM Etomoxir to the sample wells (blank receives 500 µL XF assay medium), incubate 30–60 min at 37 °C without CO₂ before loading.

steps.title: Load Plate and Run XF Analyzer
steps.instruction:
Calibrate and equilibrate the XF24 analyzer, load the prepared plate, and run the following protocols:
• TLR‑induced assay: inject port A with the chosen TLR agonist (LPS 100 ng mL⁻¹, CpG‑DNA 10 µM, IMQ 50 µg mL⁻¹, etc.) at the volume specified in the assay design, mix 3 min, wait 2 min, measure 3 min; repeat mixing/wait/measure cycles as programmed.
• Mitochondrial stress test: inject port A oligomycin (add 560 µL to achieve 0.25 µM final), mix 3 min, wait 2 min, measure 3 min; inject port B FCCP (add 624 µL for 4 µM final), repeat; inject port C rotenone + antimycin (add 681 µL for 1 µM final), repeat.
• Glycolysis stress test: inject port A glucose (add 56 µL for 10 mM final), mix/wait/measure; inject port B oligomycin (add 620 µL for 0.25 µM final); inject port C 2‑DG (add 685 µL for 50 mM final). All mixing steps are 3 min, waits 2 min, measurements 3 min. End the run after the final measurement.

steps.title: Analyze Data with Wave Software
steps.instruction: Open the assay result file in Agilent Seahorse Wave Desktop, select OCR or ECAR, normalize each well to cell number or protein concentration, export the data to Microsoft Excel or GraphPad Prism, and perform statistical analysis as described in the figure legends.

description: Immunometabolism is an emerging field of investigation at the interface between the historically distinct disciplines of immunology and metabolism (Mathis and Shoelson, 2011). Recent studies on immunometabolism in myeloid dendritic cells (mDCs) provide new insights on the mechanism of the critical controllers of innate and adaptive immunity (Pearce and Everts, 2014) (O'Neill and Pearce, 2015). In particular, extracellular flux (XF) analysis has become a standard method to measure bioenergetic functions in DCs (Everts et al., 2012) (Everts et al., 2014) (Pantel et al., 2014) (Pelgrom et al., 2016). This protocol comprises several methods to quantify the energy utilization of DCs in real-time using a Seahorse extracellular flux analyzer. The basic protocol describes a standard test with an XFe24 analyzer. If you use an XFe96 analyzer, you should adjust the number of DCs and the volume of buffer used according to the XFe96 analyzer. Please check the latest information on the Agilent website (https://www.agilent.com/en/product/cell-analysis/real-time-cell-metabolic-analysis) before your experiments. In this protocol, we mainly described the analytical methods using mouse bone marrow-derived DCs (BMDCs). If you are using other cell types, please refer to Table 1.
